answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may submit bids, with one vote per locked token rather than one per account. Splitting funds across a thousand aliases then creates no extra influence: the attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens, paying opportunity cost and risking slashing if those agents misbehave. Honest agents can still compare bids for comet, knoll, or oasis tasks, while the lock makes mass identities expensive rather than merely easy to mint.
